'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**[[2021 evacuation from Afghanistan]]
***[[Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan (2020–2021)|Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan]], [[Operation Allies Refuge]]
****[[United States Marine Corps|Marine Corps]] [[General (United States)|General]] [[Kenneth F. McKenzie Jr.]] announces that the final [[United States Armed Forces|American troops]] have left [[Afghanistan]], concluding [[United States|U.S.]] involvement in the [[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|Afghanistan war]]. [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] also confirms the end of the war in a statement. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/08/30/world/asia/afghanistan-us-occupation-ends.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.abc10.com/article/news/nation-world/biden-statement-afghanistan-evacuation/507-4075024d-3389-425e-ad28-191057f3ab66 (KXTV-TV)]
****[[United States Army|Army]] General [[Christopher T. Donahue]] becomes the last American servicemember to leave Afghanistan. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/aug/31/last-man-out-the-haunting-image-of-americas-final-moments-in-afghanistan (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Taliban]] spokesman [[Zabiullah Mujahid]] says that yesterday's [[airstrike]] by the United States killed civilians and that if "there was any potential threat in [[Afghanistan]], it should have been reported to us, not an arbitrary attack that has resulted in civilian casualties". [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2021/08/30/drone-civilians-islamic-state/ (''The Washington Post'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/taliban-condemns-us-drone-attack-kabul-chinese-state-tv-2021-08-30/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Video games in China]], [[Video game addiction in China]]
**[[China]]'s [[General Administration of Press and Publication]] announces new regulations prohibiting youth under the age of 18 years old from playing [[Online game|online video games]] for more than three hours per week, citing physical and mental health concerns. Playing of online video games will only be allowed between 8:00 pm and 9:00 pm on weekends and holidays. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/08/30/china-to-ban-kids-from-playing-online-games-for-more-than-three-hours-per-week.html (CNBC)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Hurricane Ida]] is downgraded to a [[tropical storm]] after battering the U.S. state of [[Louisiana]]. Governor [[John Bel Edwards]] urges citizens "to remain where you are" as the storm left heavy damage in the state. Heavy rains and winds are also expected in the [[Tennessee Valley|Tennessee]] and [[Ohio River|Ohio]] valleys as the storm moves further north. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2021/08/30/hurricane-ida-live-updates/ (''The Washington Post'')] [https://edition.cnn.com/us/live-news/ida-updates-08-30-21/index.html (CNN)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education]]
****[[Jakarta]] reopens schools for some students for the first time after 18 months of [[remote learning]] with enhanced safety and health measures as the [[Community Activities Restrictions Enforcement|community activities restrictions]] are eased in some regions of the country. [https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2021/aug/30/children-return-to-school-in-jakarta-as-indonesia-eases-covid-restrictions (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Prime Minister of Malaysia|Prime Minister]] [[Ismail Sabri Yaakob]] enters [[quarantine]] following a close contact with a COVID-19 patient. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/30/malaysian-pm-in-quarantine-after-contact-with-covid-19-patient (Al Jazeera English)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] reports a record 22,366 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,976,202. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/coronavirus-cases-philippines-august-30-2021 (Rappler)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] reports a record 14,224 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 449,489. [https://vietnamnews.vn/society/1022367/record-of-14224-new-covid-19-cases-announced-on-monday.html (Viet Nam News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New South Wales]]
*****[[New South Wales]] reports a record 1,290 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://www.9news.com.au/national/coronavirus-nsw-update-latest-covid-19-case-numbers-august-30-pfizer-eligibility-opens/2b36a31f-74c8-4417-9be7-560bdaa4ce66 (9 News)]
****[[Australia]] surpasses 1,000 deaths from [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.news.com.au/national/covid19-deaths-in-australia-pass-1000-as-nsw-delta-outbreak-worsens/news-story/8dae0c458bcf9e87f0b90d73ac842c4f (News.com.au)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in New Zealand]]
****[[New Zealand]] reports its first death related to the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] in a woman who died after suffering [[myocarditis]], a rare side-effect of the vaccine. [https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/new-zealand/nz-woman-dies-after-suffering-rare-side-effect-pfizer-covid-19-vaccine (TVNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic]]
***The [[Government of the Czech Republic|Czech government]] announces that the [[Czech Republic|country]] will begin offering a [[booster dose]] of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] from September 20 to all people who previously have been vaccinated at least eight months ago using either [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer]] or [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|Moderna]] vaccines. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/czechs-offer-booster-vaccine-shot-all-after-eight-months-2021-08-30/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]], [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2]]
***Scientists in [[South Africa]] detect a new variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] called C.1.2 which is associated with increased transmissibility and the ability to evade [[Antibody|antibodies]]. The variant was first identified in [[Gauteng]] and [[Mpumalanga]] provinces and has spread to seven countries as of August 13. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-08-30/new-covid-variant-found-in-south-africa-has-concerning-mutations (Bloomberg)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Nuclear power in North Korea]]
**The [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] says that [[North Korea]] appears to have restarted its [[Nyongbyon Nuclear Scientific Research Center|Nyongbyon nuclear reactor]] in a breach of the [[September 2018 inter-Korean summit]] declaration and [[United Nations Security Council]] resolutions. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-58380547 (BBC News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*Armed gang members take [[hostage]]s during their getaway following three [[bank robbery|bank robberies]] in [[Araçatuba]], [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo]], [[Brazil]]. Three people are killed during the incident, including two civilians and one of the robbers. Four other people are wounded, including one during an explosion. Three suspects have been arrested. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-58382410 (BBC News)]
*[[Kira Yarmysh]], the official spokeswoman for incarcerated [[Russians|Russian]] activist [[Alexei Navalny]], leaves Russia, reportedly travelling to [[Helsinki]], [[Finland]], after a court sentenced her to a restriction of movements for 18 months due to alleged breaches of COVID-19 restrictions. [https://www.reuters.com/world/kremlin-critic-navalnys-spokeswoman-leaves-russia-interfax-2021-08-30/ (Reuters)]
